extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, applicants, and patent examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing who may represent an applicant or patent owner, how correspondence addresses and contact information are provided/changed, signature requirements on filings, and procedures when practitioners or inventors die, are unavailable, or are suspended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to supply correspondence address and daytime telephone
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing a patent application, the applicant must specify a correspondence address to which the Office will send notices, letters and other communications. Pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.33(a) requests submission of a daytime telephone number of the party to whom correspondence is to be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The correspondence address must appear either in an application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76) or in a clearly identifiable manner elsewhere in papers submitted with the filing. While business is conducted on the written record (37 CFR 1.2), a daytime telephone number is useful to initiate contact that can later be reduced to writing. The telephone number may be changed by any party who can change the correspondence address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office selection order when multiple correspondence addresses are submitted
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one correspondence address is specified on filing, the Office will select one of the correspondence addresses for use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection order: (A) application data sheet (ADS); (B) application transmittal; (C) oath or declaration (unless power of attorney is more current); (D) power of attorney. If more than one correspondence address is specified in a single document, the Office will select the address associated with a Customer Number over a typed correspondence address. This covers situations like differing addresses on a transmittal letter versus an oath/declaration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may change correspondence address (prior to filing of § 1.63 oath/declaration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to filing of a § 1.63 oath or declaration by any of the inventors, the correspondence address may be changed by the party who filed the application; if the application was filed by a patent practitioner, any other patent practitioner named in the transmittal papers may also change the correspondence address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, before a § 1.63 oath/declaration is filed, the inventor(s), any patent practitioner named in the transmittal papers, or a party who will be the assignee who filed the application, may change the correspondence address under this paragraph. A registered practitioner named only in letterhead is not sufficient; individual must be clearly identified as a representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may change correspondence address (after § 1.63 oath/declaration filed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a § 1.63 oath or declaration has been filed by any of the inventors, the correspondence address may be changed by the parties set forth in paragraph (b) of the section (except for paragraph (b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (b) (see elsewhere) identifies who may sign amendments and thus who may effect certain changes once an oath/declaration is filed. Where a correspondence address was set pursuant to pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.33(a)(1) (prior to filing of the pre-AIA oath/declaration), that correspondence address remains in effect upon filing of the pre-AIA oath/declaration and can then only be changed pursuant to pre-AIA 37 CFR 1.33(a)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and papers must be signed by authorized persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and other papers filed in the application must be signed by one of the authorized signatories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized signatories: (1) a patent practitioner of record appointed in compliance with § 1.32(b); (2) a patent practitioner not of record who acts in a representative capacity under § 1.34; (3) an assignee as provided under § 3.71(b); or (4) all of the applicants (§ 1.41(b)) for patent, unless there is an assignee of the entire interest and such assignee has taken action in accordance with § 3.71. (Note: exceptions exist for written assertions under § 1.27(c)(2)(ii).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and correspondence rules in reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: All notices, official letters, and other communications for the patent owner(s) in a reexamination proceeding will be directed to the correspondence address; amendments and other papers must be signed by authorized parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments in a reexamination proceeding on behalf of the patent owner must be signed by the patent owner (or by all owners if more than one), or by an attorney or agent of record in the patent file, or by a registered attorney or agent not of record who acts in a representative capacity under § 1.34. The Office will not undertake double correspondence with both the patent owner(s) and the patent owner’s attorney/agent, or with more than one attorney/agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change of correspondence address during enforceable life of patent; fee address
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'correspondence address' or change thereto may be filed with the USPTO during the enforceable life of the patent and will be used in any correspondence relating to maintenance fees unless a separate 'fee address' has been specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See § 1.363 for use of 'fee address' solely for maintenance fee purposes. A change of address filed in an application or patent does not change the address for a patent practitioner in the roster of patent attorneys and agents (see § 11.11); the attorney/agent roster must be updated separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers of attorney to firms not recognized; firm's address usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Powers of attorney to firms are not recognized by the USPTO, but a firm's address may be used for the correspondence address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The address should be formatted to identify the inventor 'in care of' the firm (example provided). Patent practitioners are reminded that updating the attorney/agent roster is separate from filing a change of address in individual applications. See MPEP § 601.03 for change of correspondence address procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two patent practitioners for same application — correspondence designation and effect of later-filed POA
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant simultaneously appoints two patent practitioners, the applicant should indicate with whom correspondence is to be conducted by specifying a correspondence address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a second practitioner is later added by submitting a new power of attorney that appoints both practitioners, correspondence will be mailed to the correspondence address of record. If a later-filed power of attorney lists only the second practitioner, that later-filed power of attorney serves as a revocation of the earlier-filed power of attorney even without an express revocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing of papers by registered practitioners not of record (37 CFR 1.34) does not by itself authorize interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered attorneys/agents not of record may file papers in applications under 37 CFR 1.34, and such filings are considered representation with respect to the concurrent filing only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a paper that is not related to an interview does not show authorization to conduct an interview. To show authorization to act in a representative capacity for purposes of conducting an interview, a registered practitioner should complete, sign, and file an Applicant Initiated Interview Request Form (PTOL-413A). Alternatively, Form PTO/SB/84 'Authorization to Act in a Representative Capacity' may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design patent practitioners and use of 37 CFR 1.34 for interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Design patent practitioners can only use acting in a representative capacity under 37 CFR 1.34 to show authorization to conduct interviews in design patent matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The use of 37 CFR 1.34 by a third party or its representative to conduct interviews or take other actions not specifically permitted by the rules is considered a violation of 37 CFR 11.18 and may result in disciplinary action if done by a practitioner. See MPEP §§ 402.04 and 1502.02 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office encouragement of interviews with practitioner of record and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office encourages use of interviews to expedite prosecution; when the examiner believes progress would be advanced, the examiner may contact the patent practitioner of record to suggest a telephonic, personal, or video conference interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered attorneys or agents not of record who act under 37 CFR 1.34 should not be contacted for restriction requirements or approval of examiner's amendments. Non-registered, suspended, or excluded representatives should not be contacted regarding an application unless the application belongs to that attorney/agent. See MPEP § 713 for interview procedures, § 812.01 for telephone restriction practice, and § 405 for interviews with a practitioner not of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-initiated interview procedures (PTOL-413A)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicant initiates an interview, an Applicant Initiated Interview Request form (PTOL-413A) should be submitted to the examiner prior to the interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form should identify participants, proposed date, whether personal/telephonic/video, and include a brief description of issues to be discussed so the examiner can prepare and focus the interview. See MPEP §§ 713.01 and 713.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of death of patent practitioner on power of attorney and correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The power of attorney of a patent practitioner will be revoked or terminated by his or her death; the practitioner may not appoint a 'substitute' whose power is intended to survive the practitioner's death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If notification of the death of the sole practitioner of record is received, correspondence continues to be held with the office of the deceased practitioner but a copy of the Office action is mailed to the person who originally appointed the practitioner. Examiner should add form paragraph 4.03 notifying of death and advising that a new registered attorney or agent may be appointed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspended or excluded practitioner — power ineffective and mailing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any power of attorney given to a practitioner who has been suspended or disbarred by the Office is ineffective and does not authorize the person to practice before the Office or represent applicants/patentees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office does not communicate with suspended or excluded practitioners. Use form paragraphs 4.07 and 4.08 depending on whether the suspended practitioner is sole or one of plural practitioners. Where no remaining practitioner of record exists, Office action is mailed to the applicant first named in the application at current address of record. If at least one practitioner remains of record, mail to that practitioner and to the applicant as appropriate. Examiner Notes provide bracket instructions for form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature requirements when no practitioner of record (before and after Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: Signature rules differ depending on filing date relative to Sept 16, 2012: before that date (pre-AIA) and on/after that date (AIA changes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed before Sept 16, 2012: papers must be signed by (1) all named applicants unless one has power of attorney of record; or (2) if partial assignee of record exists, by all named applicants retaining interest and such assignee; or (3) if assignee of entire interest, by such assignee; or (4) by a registered patent attorney or agent not of record who acts under 37 CFR 1.34. For applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012: papers must be signed by (1) a patent practitioner of record; (2) a patent practitioner not of record who acts under 37 CFR 1.34; or (3) the applicant, except that papers submitted on behalf of a juristic entity applicant must be signed by a patent practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution options when inventor is deceased or legally incapacitated (35 U.S.C. 117; 37 CFR 1.43)
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal representatives of deceased or legally incapacitated inventors may make application for patent and letters patent may be issued to the legal representative upon proper intervention; a substitute statement may be executed in lieu of an oath/declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.64 and MPEP § 604 concerning execution of a substitute statement by a legal representative in lieu of an oath or declaration. Proof of authority of a legal representative is not required by the Office, though such representatives should ensure they are properly acting in that capacity. If administrator/executor discharged and new application desired, new letters of administration may be necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of power of attorney upon death of inventor (unless coupled with interest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless a power of attorney is coupled with an interest (e.g., practitioner is assignee or part-assignee), the death of an inventor who is an applicant party terminates the power of attorney given by the deceased inventor in an application filed on or after Sept 16, 2012 (and similar rule pre-AIA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new power from heirs, administrators, executors, or assignees is necessary if the deceased inventor is sole inventor-applicant or if all powers of attorney have been terminated. See both pre- and post-AIA versions in MPEP § 409.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution by assignee/obligated assignee/37 CFR 1.46 applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.46, a person to whom the inventor assigned (assignee), to whom inventor was under obligation to assign (obligated assignee), or a person who shows sufficient proprietary interest may make application on behalf of deceased or incapacitated inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the 37 CFR 1.46 applicant is the assignee or obligated assignee or shows sufficient proprietary interest, no need to involve legal representative; the 37 CFR 1.46 applicant can execute the substitute statement. See MPEP § 409.05 and 37 CFR 1.64 for substitute statement execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution where surviving joint inventor-applicants continue after co-inventor's death
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is prosecuted by joint inventor-applicants without a power of attorney and a joint inventor dies after filing, the living joint inventor(s) who are applicants must submit proof that the other is dead; upon such proof, only signatures of living joint inventor-applicants are required unless the legal representative intervenes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If legal representative intervenes, they must submit a substitute statement in compliance with 37 CFR 1.64. Once legal representative intervenes, signatures of living joint inventors and legal representative are required until a representative is appointed. These rules apply to both pre- and post-Sept 16, 2012 filings with noted differences elsewhere in MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unavailable or refusing joint inventor — substitute statement and petition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Joint inventors must apply jointly and each make the inventor's oath/declaration (37 CFR 1.63), except as provided in 37 CFR 1.64. If a joint inventor refuses to join or cannot be found/reached after diligent effort, the other joint inventor(s) may make the application on behalf of themselves and the omitted inventor and must address substitute statement/petition requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-AIA: submit substitute statement under 37 CFR 1.64 as discussed in MPEP § 604. Pre-AIA (37 CFR 1.47): the application may be made by the other inventor on behalf of the nonsigning inventor, but the oath/declaration must be accompanied by a petition including proof of pertinent facts, the fee set forth in § 1.17(g), and the last known address of the nonsigning inventor. Director may prescribe notice to the omitted inventor and terms for granting the patent to the applying inventor.
